subject: TTFT & streaming cadence — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming cadence — post-demo next steps

Alex — great chat earlier, thanks for the time and for walking us through the Acme AI use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance/SLO side so we can scope a short technical run:  

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary app: interactive mobile chat + web console
- Desired TTFT target: sub-second preferred (you mentioned ~200–300ms goal)
- Streaming requirements: prefer WebSocket for mobile (SSE fallback for web); chunk cadence target ~150–250ms
- Peak concurrency: ~100–150 concurrent sessions during spikes; sustained throughput ~30–50 qps
- Typical prompt size: 60–120 tokens; max context ~2,048 tokens

What we need from you to scope a perf run:
1) Confirm the TTFT measurement you want (time-to-first-token as observed by the server vs end-to-end client)
2) Share representative sample payloads (prompts + metadata)
3) Confirm preferred protocol (WebSocket primary, SSE fallback?)
4) Any hard SLOs for chunk cadence (min/max latency between chunks) and acceptable first-chunk size (tokens/bytes)

I've attached a one-page template to capture these (acme-ttft-template.xlsx) — if you can fill that and send sample payloads we can  schedule a short 30–60 minute perf run with our infra team (Ethan + Vivek) and come back with measured TTFT and chunk cadence numbers.  

Proposed next steps:
- You populate the template + sample payloads (today if possible)
- We run a targeted perf test (WebSocket streaming) + SSE fallback test: 30 min each
- We share a short report with TTFT percentiles (p50/p90/p99), average chunk cadence, and recommended runtime config (batching, kv-cache policy, quantization suggestion)

Linking the HubSpot deal and demo recording here for context: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-12345 and https://redwood.cloud/recordings/demo-20260627

Thanks — happy to join a quick call to walk through the template.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>

Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — post-demo next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side (answers inline):

> Desired TTFT target: sub-second preferred (you mentioned ~200–300ms goal)
- Confirmed: our internal product team is targeting <= 300ms time-to-first-token from the server edge for mobile. If we can hit ~200ms that's ideal, but 300ms is the SLO target.

> Streaming requirements: prefer WebSocket for mobile (SSE fallback for web); chunk cadence target ~150–250ms
- We prefer WebSocket for the mobile app. SSE is fine for the web console. Chunk cadence target: we want chunks delivered roughly every 150–300ms; 150ms is preferred for a snappy experience, but up to 300ms is acceptable in heavy-network conditions. First-chunk size: ~10–30 tokens typically.

> Peak concurrency: ~100–150 concurrent sessions during spikes; sustained throughput ~30–50 qps
- Confirmed peak concurrent users 120 (estimate). Sustained throughput 40 qps, with short spikes up to 80 qps for 2–5 minutes.

Prompt sizes: typical ~80 tokens, worst-case up to 800 tokens when we include context.

I'm attaching a small sample payload bundle and the template filled with our best estimates (acme-sample-payloads.json). We'll also add device/network breakdowns in the spreadsheet where helpful.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Sr. Product Manager, Acme AI

Alex — perfect, this is exactly what we need. A couple of quick clarifications and a proposed mutual action plan:  

Clarify TTFT measurement: we typically report TTFT as time from request receipt at the Redwood edge to emission of the first token from the model runtime (server-side). That excludes client render time and network retransmits. If you need an end-to-end client-measured TTFT, we can run a small set of client-side measurements as a follow-up. Which would you prefer for the initial SLO assessment?

Perf-run proposal (we can kick off as soon as you send the payloads):
- Day 0: receive sample payloads + filled template
- Day 1: 30-minute WebSocket streaming test @ sustained 40 qps with 120 concurrent sessions simulated (short spike up to 80 qps)
- Day 1: 30-minute SSE fallback test for the web console
- Deliverable: report with p50/p90/p99 TTFT, chunk cadence distribution, per-route recommended runtime config (batch size, latency targets, quantization suggestions)

Technical notes for Ethan/Vivek:
- We'll measure TTFT both including and excluding model warm-start time. If prompts require large context (>512 tokens), batching behavior will differ; we'll include a recommended config.

Next steps / owners:
- Alex: send sample payloads + completed template (today if possible) — Alex
- Ethan/Vivek: run the perf tests and capture traces + TTFT percentiles — Ethan/Vivek
- Marissa: compile report and share with product + infra — Marissa

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up after the perf run to review results.

—Marissa
